name: Desktop Browser Access Dialog
description: Owns installation-scoped Personal Access Token creation and reset together with explicit loopback and trusted-local-network Browser access controls.

states: Inspect the stopped state, missing-token creation action, and the unencrypted HTTP warning before enabling local-network preview.
Inspect active trusted-LAN access with a configured token, exact origins, per-address copy actions, and immediate revocation.
Inspect the one-time Personal Access Token disclosure, explicit copy action, and reset affordance.

useWhen: The Desktop process must explicitly start, inspect, switch, or revoke process-lifetime Browser access.
A user needs to create or reset the Personal Access Token used by Browser sign-in.
A trusted local network needs an HTTP preview address with full terminal control and an explicit warning.
avoidWhen: A Browser-connected Gateway page is already consuming access and must not gain listener lifecycle authority.
Internet exposure, TLS termination, multi-user accounts, public IP publication, or a background service is required.
invariants: Browser access begins stopped and loopback is the default start mode; local-network binding requires an explicit user action.
Browser access cannot start until an installation-scoped Personal Access Token has been created.
A new Personal Access Token is shown once; reset stops access and invalidates every Browser session before replacing the verifier.
The dialog receives only sanitized origins, bounded failure codes, and the one-time issued token, never a signed session credential or complete access URL.
Access-link copy and system-Browser open effects remain Main-owned and are available only for active exact origins.
Local-network preview always presents the unencrypted HTTP and full-terminal-control warning and offers immediate revocation.
